answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie every identity to a decaying reputation bond: each agent locks a small stake that earns trust only through verified work over time, like an ember that must be tended to stay lit. A sudden gale of fresh accounts cannot buy history — their bonds start cold and their influence stays near zero until a steady pulse of completed, peer-attested tasks proves them real. If an agent misbehaves, the bond is slashed and its accumulated standing burns away, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes and buys no shortcut to trust.
